question: Why might a burn suffered at night heal more slowly than one suffered by day?
answer: Skin cells keep time. Hoyle and colleagues found the body clock in fibroblasts, the cells that rebuild skin, sets how readily they enter a wound, through daily swings in actin, the protein that powers crawling. In a burns database, night injuries took about 60% longer to heal. Cells in a dish kept the rhythm.
move: When the hour changes an outcome, ask what inside is keeping time.
source: Hoyle et al., Science Translational Medicine, 2017
